reason: Both pages get the numbers right: 14 of 72 right for the cheap model, all holds; 58 escalations; break-even $0.0011 for ask twice and $0.133 for Claude review; $500/$405/$662 at $0.05 and 10,000 invoices. A gives them in a tight seven-step lesson at phone width. The dots split 14/58 in step 3, step 4 shows the bill at 5 cents, step 5 shows where each line crosses zero, step 6 gives a slider plus volume buttons, and step 7 gives takeaways with uncertainty (12-30% skipped, Claude break-even $0.086-$0.217). B has more depth: a per-invoice grid with tap tooltips, the break-even formula written out, a log-scale price slider with presets, the cheap-only and person-review routes, and a full caveats list. But its fifth step, the one that makes the decision, overflows the card at 390 px: the title, body text, the 'Try a price' button, the grid and the 19.4% tile are all clipped. Its saving chart also has unreadably small text on a phone. A's clean, focused delivery at phone width decided it.

A: The interactive chart's linear $0-$0.30 x-axis squeezes the ask-twice break-even ($0.0011) into the origin, so that crossing cannot be seen, only read from a label.
At the slider extremes labels collide: at $0.30 / 100,000 the 'Ask twice' line label fades under '+$5,812'; at $0.0005 the '-$26' label sits on the x-axis '$0' tick.
The slider's keyboard step is very fine (30 arrow presses move $0.050 to $0.065) and volume offers only 1k/10k/100k. The cheap-model-alone route appears only as a 'not drawn' note in step 4.
B: Step 5 of the stepper overflows its card at 390 px (text column 416 px inside a 356 px overflow-hidden panel). The heading, paragraphs, the 'Try a price' button, the right column of the invoice grid and the '19.4% calls saved' tile are all clipped.
The monthly-saving chart's axis and annotation text is about 6-7 px at phone width and hard to read. In dark mode the legend swatch for 'Dark part: expensive calls' is drawn light.

Edge handling and wording: an empty or negative volume silently becomes '1 invoices'. At the 'Review break-even' preset the summary says the reviewer 'would cost $0.052 more... needs a price above $0.133' while the price reads $0.133. No interval is given for the 14/72 share that drives every saving.
